title: 2nd & 15 2026 Preseason Power Rankings
methodology: 2nd & 15 editorial ranking. The approved Top 10 and first five out are preserved from the produced episode; ranks 16-32 use a blended editorial and market view from DAZN, PFT and Kalshi.

rankings.headline: Star power and balance
rankings.summary: The most complete roster in the ranking, with elite coaching, premium talent and fewer obvious weaknesses than the other contenders.

rankings.headline: Championship identity
rankings.summary: The defending champions retain a deep roster, a physical identity and enough continuity to remain near the top.

rankings.headline: Built for January
rankings.summary: Strength along both lines, explosive playmakers and organizational depth give Philadelphia one of the league's safest postseason profiles.

rankings.headline: Elite quarterback play travels
rankings.summary: Josh Allen keeps Buffalo's floor and ceiling high while a reworked supporting cast and coaching structure settle into place.

rankings.headline: Lamar changes every game
rankings.summary: Lamar Jackson and a talented defense preserve a championship ceiling, but a major leadership transition creates real uncertainty.

rankings.headline: Defense sets the floor
rankings.summary: Continuity, a strong defense and one of the league's better supporting structures keep Denver close to the top five.

rankings.headline: Expectations have arrived
rankings.summary: New England has momentum and a rapidly improved roster, but must prove last season's success is repeatable against a tougher schedule.

rankings.headline: The ceiling remains high
rankings.summary: High-end talent, veteran leadership and a proven system remain in place, but health and age make the floor less secure.

rankings.headline: Elite defense, offensive questions
rankings.summary: Houston's defense can carry a contender, but the offense and C.J. Stroud must consistently hold up against championship-level competition.

rankings.headline: Never count out Mahomes
rankings.summary: Patrick Mahomes preserves a championship ceiling, but health, protection and roster turnover keep Kansas City outside the top tier for now.

rankings.headline: Healthy protection changes everything
rankings.summary: Justin Herbert and a healthy tackle duo give the Chargers top-ten upside, while interior protection remains the biggest concern.

rankings.headline: Year two could unlock the offense
rankings.summary: Caleb Williams, Ben Johnson and a young group of playmakers give Chicago major upside if their growth turns into week-to-week consistency.

rankings.headline: The offense remains dangerous
rankings.summary: Detroit still has premium offensive talent, but the defense needs more pressure production beyond Aidan Hutchinson.

rankings.headline: Talent with something to prove
rankings.summary: Jacksonville has playoff-level talent and late-season momentum, but must replace key departures and prove its best stretch was sustainable.

rankings.headline: A playoff core with early hurdles
rankings.summary: Jordan Love and Micah Parsons keep Green Bay competitive, but availability and several meaningful departures lower the preseason floor.

rankings.headline: The offense may need heroics
rankings.summary: Joe Burrow and an elite group of weapons can outscore almost anyone, but the rebuilt defense has to compensate for major losses.

rankings.headline: Average defense could be enough
rankings.summary: Dallas has a playoff-caliber offense; the season depends on whether its defensive additions can raise a weak unit to league average.

rankings.headline: Defense keeps them relevant
rankings.summary: A dangerous edge group and veteran quarterback give Pittsburgh a path, though the offensive line and overall scoring ceiling remain concerns.

rankings.headline: A quarterback reset with real weapons
rankings.summary: Minnesota's receiving talent and intriguing defensive front provide upside if its new quarterback setup stabilizes quickly.

rankings.headline: Talent remains, consistency does not
rankings.summary: Tampa Bay still has useful offensive pieces, but must overcome major veteran departures and the inconsistency that defined last season.
concerns: Replacing Mike Evans and Lavonte David

rankings.headline: Which version will show up?
rankings.summary: Indianapolis has a talented defense and showed real offensive promise before collapsing, leaving a wide range of possible outcomes.

rankings.headline: Growth depends on protection
rankings.summary: Bryce Young and an improved defense provide optimism, but offensive-line losses could limit the next step.

rankings.headline: Strong weapons, unanswered questions
rankings.summary: Atlanta's offensive weapons and secondary create upside, but quarterback consistency and pass-rush availability hold the team back.

rankings.headline: A young core worth watching
rankings.summary: A promising offensive nucleus, improved line and new coaching direction give New York upset potential despite limited proof.

rankings.headline: The quarterback raises the ceiling
rankings.summary: Jayden Daniels and proven receivers can outperform this ranking, but offensive-line health and overall depth remain major concerns.

rankings.headline: Moving forward, not there yet
rankings.summary: New Orleans made sensible additions, but the quarterback's supporting cast and the defensive front remain short of contender level.

rankings.headline: Built more for the future
rankings.summary: Tennessee has several blue-chip building blocks, but the offensive line and broader roster still look a year away.

rankings.headline: Foundation pieces, major gaps
rankings.summary: Maxx Crosby, Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty form a useful foundation, but quarterback, receiver and pass-rush depth remain unresolved.

rankings.headline: Still searching for the quarterback
rankings.summary: Cleveland improved parts of the line and retains defensive talent, but no quarterback has provided a trustworthy answer.

rankings.headline: A transition year
rankings.summary: The Jets have promising young trench pieces and useful defensive additions, but the roster is structured more for development than winning now.

rankings.headline: Too many projections, not enough proof
rankings.summary: De'Von Achane and several young players offer hope, but Miami lacks enough proven difference-makers across the roster.

rankings.headline: The rebuild has a long runway
rankings.summary: A difficult division, quarterback transition, offensive-line injury and thin defense make Arizona the league's least complete team entering the season.
